disagreements.topic: Pipeline value (LM expansion, Lake Hawkeye, Muskie, Chesapeake)
disagreements.positions: Per share: agent_3 ~$0.07 net (NPV ~$0.94M/MW today at 11%, wiped out by Muskie collateral/liabilities and the Chesapeake price); agent_1 $2.09 (12m fwd); agent_4 $2.58 (horizon; ~$3.65M/MW today at 10%); agent_2 $2.65; agent_5 $3.03 (Lake Hawkeye 20%, Chesapeake 25%/$0.72). Yields on cost assumed: agent_1/agent_3 ~13.5%, agent_5 ~14.5%, agent_4 ~15%, agent_2 ~15.7%.
disagreements.resolution: Now the largest single source of dispersion ($0.1-3.0/share, more than the split-vs-single rate effect of ~$0.7-1.4). Company evidence is mixed: the Q2 deck says 'low-teens yield on cost', while the CFO and CEO on the Q2 call say they target 'mid-teens'. No pipeline site has a tenant; NY sites face EO 62 and the Lansing draft ban; Chesapeake has not closed (no 8-K or release through Oct 2). I leave each agent's pipeline in place (all are probability-weighted, net of $10-12.5M/MW capex, at WACC as the brief requires) but treat the ~13-14% yield (deck) as the better-sourced centre, so agent_4/agent_5/agent_2 sit at the generous end and agent_3 at the harsh end.
disagreements.evidence: Q2-26 investor deck (playbook slide: 'Low-teens yield on cost'); Q2-26 call (CFO: 'mid-teens return'); IR press-release list checked Oct 2 2026 (latest release Aug 24).

disagreements.positions: agent_1 and agent_2 $4.06B (treat $4.0-4.5B as including the $200M site and deduct the full $353M contributed); agent_3 $4.2B; agent_4 the full $4.41B from 6/30/26 (ignores the $353M already spent); agent_5 ~$4.4B total incl. site (~$3.95B from Q4'26).
disagreements.resolution: The KY PSC release says $10-12M per MW, '~$4.0-4.5 billion of investment in site development and the initial data halls'. That wording covers development, not the $200M land purchase. So capex to go at 6/30/26 = 401 MW x $11M ($4.41B) less the ~$153M non-land part of the $353M contributed = ~$4.26B. agent_1/agent_2 are ~$0.2B too low; agent_4 is ~$0.15B too high (it charges spend already out of June-30 cash); agent_5 ~$0.2B too low; agent_3 about right.
disagreements.evidence: TeraWulf release Aug 24 2026 (KY PSC approves 482 MW); Q2-26 call (CFO: '~$353 million of equity as of June 30, including the $200 million site acquisition cost').

disagreements.resolution: The 10-Q (Note 11) confirms a fixed-amount put from the first anniversary of operations, less distributions, with the figure undisclosed. The only number filed is the $100.6M acquisition-date fair value, which is a residual (net assets less $200M cash). Reconciled for every agent: ~$150M payable around the first operations anniversary (~end-2028), PV ~$0.13B today. If the put is not redeemed, the seller keeps 6.8% and must then fund capital, so a max(put, 6.8% of equity) floor is not needed. Effect versus agents: -$0.03 to +$0.14/share.
disagreements.evidence: Q2-26 10-Q Note 3 (consideration table: NCI fair value $100,588k) and Note 11 (Justified Data Campus Developer: fixed-amount put, capital-contribution clause).

disagreements.positions: agent_1 $150M x 85%, net of ~$50M for the 210 MW plant; agent_2 $150M x 90% plus ~$10M/yr of generation; agent_4 $150M x 85%, no plant value; agent_3 $200M x 85% less $80M plant; agent_5 $200M 'net' x 90%.
disagreements.resolution: The price is not in the 10-Q, the FY25 10-K, the Q2 deck or the call; the CFO says it is funded from existing liquidity. Reconciled for every agent: $175M (midpoint of the agents' $150-200M), 85% closing odds, less ~$65M for the operating 210 MW plant, for an expected net cost of ~$94M (~$0.15/share). Effect versus agents: -$0.02 to +$0.14/share (agent_5 most).
disagreements.evidence: Q2-26 10-Q Note 1 (Morgantown Purchase Agreement, FERC authorization Jul 29 2026, close expected 2H26, no price); Q2-26 call (funded from liquidity).

disagreements.positions: Google-backstopped Fluidstack rent: agent_5 7.75%, agent_2 8.0%, agent_1 and agent_4 8.5%, agent_3 8.7%. Unbacked Fluidstack: 9.0-10.25%, except agent_4, which puts all Fluidstack rent (incl. the 56% unbacked) at 8.5%. Core42: 9.0-10.25%. Anthropic: 9.25-9.75%. WACC 10-11%.
disagreements.resolution: All anchor on the WULF Compute $3.2B 7.75% notes (8.7% effective; Ba2/BB/BB), secured on exactly these leases and sized to the $3.2B Google backstop, with read-across from Abernathy at 7.25% and Hut 8's IG project notes. Only agent_4 breaks the brief by giving the unbacked 56% the backstopped rate; fixed at ~9.5% (about -$0.20/share). agent_5's 7.75% equals the notes' coupon (a debt yield) applied to an unlevered claim; it is the most aggressive but still anchored. The claimed ~6.4-6.6% secondary yield on the notes is unverified and implausibly tight for BB over a 5.24% 10-yr; no agent relies on it, and I do not.
disagreements.evidence: sites.json contracts_credit (10-Q effective rate 8.7%; ratings at issue); Q2 call (CFO illustrates ~6.5% debt / ~10% WACC).

disagreements.positions: Cash G&A: agent_4 $100M, agent_2 $120M, agent_5 $140M plus $80M/yr SBC, agent_1 $150M, agent_3 inside an 80% all-in margin.
disagreements.resolution: 10-Q: H1-26 SG&A $254.7M (incl. related party), of which ~$185M is stock comp, so cash SG&A runs ~$140M/yr. agent_5 alone charges future SBC (-$1.77/share). That is defensible because the 613M count covers only existing awards, but it explains most of agent_5's gap to the others. Not changed; flagged.
disagreements.evidence: Q2-26 10-Q income statement and equity statement.

disagreements.positions: agent_4 moved the pipeline into its DCF and also adds the same per-site values to its SOTP and EV/EBITDA legs; agent_1, agent_3 and agent_5 carry the pipeline in every method; agent_2 carries it in the DCF only (its 13x comp multiple is taken to cover optionality).
disagreements.resolution: No agent counts the pipeline more than once inside any single method, and each blend's weights sum to 1, so the pipeline carries exactly a 100% weight in every blend (agent_2: an explicit 50% plus whatever the multiple implies). agent_4's +$1.9 fair-value rise is mostly this reallocation (pipeline weight 30% to 100%), which matches its weights and is not a double count. One soft overlap: agent_4's 12x EBITDA multiple is set partly from data-center REIT multiples that embed development pipelines, and it then adds the full $1.52B pipeline. Worth at most ~$0.2 on its blend; flagged, not changed. Muskie collateral: checked in agent_2's model (only the $270M of future LOA collateral is an outflow; the $295M already posted sits in net debt), and in agents 1, 3, 4 and 5. Counted once in each.
disagreements.evidence: agents' fair_value.methods inputs; agent_2 model (collateral lines).

Possible in-window items (CB-4 commencement confirmation, Justified debt launch, Chesapeake close, a preliminary Q3 print, the Oct 28 FOMC) cut both ways, and the round-4 site and discount-rate work moves only long-dated value, so I keep the forecasters' tight mean (~0.48 at spot).

thesis_break_reason: Forecaster breaks are $5.0-7.0 (mean $5.85). Contracted-only split-rate values are ~$4.5-6.3 for four agents ($2.5 for agent_5 after SBC). A sustained close near $6 means the market gives the pipeline nothing and doubts the contracts or financing: a punitive or failed ~$3.5B Justified financing, loss of Anthropic's expected IG support, CB-4/CB-5 commencement slipping far enough to delay the Google backstop tranches, or a dilutive raise.
key_drivers: Pipeline value is now the widest disagreement ($0.1-3.0/share across agents): yield on cost (deck 'low-teens' vs call 'mid-teens'), tenant odds at Muskie and Chesapeake, and NY permitting (EO 62, Lansing draft ban)
Discount rate: the split adds ~$0.7-1.4/share over single-rate DCFs; WACC (10-11%) on post-term, terminal and pipeline flows still moves value ~$1.5-2/share per 50-100bp
